learningObjectives: Describe the value of low-code application development.
Recognize the purpose of each Pega Platform studio.
Find and use the navigation elements in App Studio.
Explain how Dev Studio differs from App Studio.
Switch between App Studio and Dev Studio when developing in Pega Platform.

elements.description: Products and cloud services that use visual, declarative techniques instead of programming. As you manipulate the visual model, tools generate the underlying code — Pega has done this for 30 years.
Low-code bridges business stakeholders and skilled developers with a common visual language, enabling teams to deliver faster, collaborate better, and focus on business logic rather than code.
The same Pega application can serve as a web page, mobile app, or chatbot; data can arrive via email or a robot. Organizations unify all channels without maintaining disparate code lines.

Visual, end-to-end tools make everyone more productive. Citizen developers create application code; experienced developers extend robust applications more rapidly, hide implementation, and build patterns once to reuse many times across the ecosystem.

elements.text: LEGO vs. injection-molding: traditional coding molds every brick from raw resin each time; low-code hands you pre-made, snap-together bricks (visual components). You assemble robust structures fast — and an expert can still craft a custom brick when the kit doesn't have one.

bulletPoints: Drag-and-drop, process flows, and visual tools let anyone build transformational software regardless of technical ability.
Through a visual interface, Pega empowers users to build integrations and graphically map data for a holistic view of the data landscape.
Real example: a marketing team replaces a shared tracking spreadsheet with an email/web request system featuring reporting, notifications, and SLA tracking.

elements.description: A low-code authoring space providing CORE features: Case design, data management, and user experience (UI). Users: citizen developers plus technical staff — application developers, front-end developers, data engineers, business analysts, and System Architects. The place to get applications operating quickly.

A low-code authoring space with ADVANCED features. Technical users: full-stack developers, System Architects, and database/security administrators. Used for complex Rule configuration, security/access control, reuse management, and performance.

An ANALYTICS space for data scientists and business decision-makers, providing features to build machine-learning models for adaptive, predictive, and text analytics. Access requires pxPredictionStudio among the Portals on the user's access group.
A software ADMINISTRATION space managed by IT for system administration — runtime information and configuration options for monitoring and debugging system resources.

elements.text: Four workbenches in one workshop: App Studio is the assembly bench (build fast), Dev Studio is the precision-tooling bench (deep config), Prediction Studio is the R&D lab (models), Admin Studio is the control room (monitoring). Pick the bench that matches the task and your expertise.

bulletPoints: Studios are ROLE-BASED authoring spaces; each provides tools aligned to the user's expertise.

Best practice: System Architects and technical members work in App Studio UNLESS a needed feature is unavailable there, because App Studio manages behind-the-scenes configuration and reduces programming errors.
Users can access one or more studios; at login the system opens the user's DEFAULT studio, then they can switch to any other studio they have access to.
Studio access is configured by granting Portal access to an Access Group.

elements.description: Every studio has three regions:
items: A Header (menus and the upper-left studio-switcher)
A Navigation pane (explorers like Case Type and Data)
An Authoring space where you configure behavior

elements.text: Depending on screen size, icons replace text-based menu options; hover over an icon to view the menu name.

bulletPoints: App Studio navigation items: Overview (Case Types & Channels at a glance), Case Types (reusable business processes), Data (information to process/resolve cases), Channels (Web/Mobile portals), Library (the Reuse Library of reusable assets), and Users (participants).
Pega Agile Workbench captures real-time feedback and tracks feature development; opened from the App Studio header.

elements.description: App Studio supports agile best practices and REAL-TIME UI design while processing work. A team testing an online-shopping UI can add fields and change controls (e.g., drop-downs) live — ideal for stakeholder reviews where feedback is implemented in real time.

Captures and presents user stories, bugs, and feedback items to support agile best practices and collaboration across technical and business members. Provides traceability from objectives to development tasks to implementation.

Instructions that govern application behavior (like the rules of chess govern the pieces). As you build visually, Pega auto-generates Rules in the background using the SAME names you choose — which is why business-friendly names matter.
Rules are organized into reusable Layers; each Layer is a unique application built on one or more others. Rulesets store, manage, and identify Rules that can be shared and reused as a whole unit.

The App Studio overview's Application Layers Widget visualizes your Rulesets and identifies the application type. Two OOTB architectures: Constellation architecture (Constellation Ruleset, new View-based UI) and Traditional UI architecture (Theme Cosmos Ruleset, Section-based UI).

bulletPoints: Best practice: use business-friendly names (e.g., 'Send email', 'Sales process') instead of 'app1' or 'field3' — Rules are auto-generated with those names and are easier to find.
Features support traceability: link development tasks (stories, work items) to a feature/objective.
You can also confirm the application type in Dev Studio via the Application Definition's 'Build on applications' section.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Dev Studio: Co-development, Reuse, and Naming

elements.description: Two groups defined by Pega for co-development:
items: DOMAIN experts (Business Analysts, Citizen Developers, front-end developers) — provide process/user insight; primarily work in App Studio
IMPLEMENTATION experts (System Architects, full-stack/DB/security admins) — handle complex configuration; primarily work in Dev Studio

elements.description: Business and IT work together: a Business Analyst designs Views in App Studio while a System Architect adds advanced logic in Dev Studio, combining domain insight with implementation expertise.

elements.term: Promote reuse by extending Rule scope
elements.description: In Dev Studio, developers access all layers and extend a rule's scope from one Case Type to an application, division, or whole organization, creating a reusable library that cuts future development time.

elements.term: Advanced SLA options in Dev Studio
elements.description: Beyond App Studio's basic goal/deadline, Dev Studio exposes:
items: Initialization behavior (custom initial urgency, delayed timer start)
Variable interval length (programmatic durations per Case)
Additional escalation actions (reassign a task or resolve a Case)

elements.text: Naming differences are a passport stamp: the SAME record crosses the border between studios but gets a different name. A 'Field' in App Studio is a 'Property' in Dev Studio — same traveler, different stamp.

bulletPoints: App Studio → Dev Studio naming: Field → Property; Goal and deadline → Service-Level Agreement (SLA); User → Operator; Team → Work Group.
Switch studios from the upper-left menu; from App Studio you can open a specific rule (e.g., an SLA) directly in Dev Studio.
Co-development pairs domain knowledge (what the business needs) with implementation expertise (how Pega delivers it).

elements.description: Pega supports many integration standards and protocols so you focus on business requirements. A standard API connector exchanges data in real time when both systems support a common protocol.
Used when no other integration is feasible — typically legacy systems with no usable API. A robot interacts with the system's UI to perform the same steps a person would, but far faster.
Automation that works ALONGSIDE a human in the process, in real time. Example: a CSR triggers a robot mid-call to update an address by driving the legacy system's UI while the customer waits.

The request is placed in a QUEUE for later background processing. Advantages: optimizes system resources, reduces peak loads, and lets the CSR keep serving the customer instead of waiting for the update to finish.
A control-tower application that lets you monitor and schedule RPA robots and provides performance analytics for all robots.

elements.text: Connector vs. RPA: a connector is a direct phone line between two systems that speak the same language; RPA hires a very fast assistant to physically type into an old system's screen because that system never got a phone line (API).

bulletPoints: Choose RPA when a system has no API, an inaccessible API, or an insufficient API; otherwise prefer a connector.

Because Pega separates application functionality from integration details (data/integration layer is separate from the Application layer), a robotic automation can later be REPLACED by a connector with minimal application impact — aligning with a strategy to unify on a single modern SOR.
Knowing when to use RPA vs. a connector maximizes return on investment.

examPitfalls.title: Counting and naming the four studios
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Questions test the exact set — App, Dev, Prediction, Admin — and which role/task each serves. Prediction (analytics/ML) and Admin (system administration) are commonly swapped.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Map each studio to purpose: App=core build, Dev=advanced config, Prediction=ML/analytics models, Admin=system monitoring/administration.

examPitfalls.title: Where technical members work by default
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A frequent trap implies System Architects default to Dev Studio. The best practice is the opposite.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Default to App Studio (it manages behind-the-scenes config and reduces errors); switch to Dev Studio only for advanced features like integration services or class mappings.

examPitfalls.title: Constellation Ruleset vs. Theme Cosmos Ruleset
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Candidates mix up which Ruleset maps to which architecture and UI model.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Constellation architecture → Constellation Ruleset → View-based UI. Traditional architecture → Theme Cosmos Ruleset → Section-based UI.

examPitfalls.title: App Studio vs. Dev Studio terminology
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Scenario questions name a record by its OTHER-studio term (Property, Operator, Work Group, SLA).
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Memorize: Field=Property, Goal and deadline=SLA, User=Operator, Team=Work Group.

examPitfalls.title: Connector vs. RPA selection
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Tests pick the wrong tool for a legacy system. RPA is for when there is NO feasible API; a connector is preferred when a standard protocol exists.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: No usable API → RPA; standard protocol available → API connector for real-time exchange.

examPitfalls.title: Attended vs. Unattended RPA
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Both can perform the same update; the difference is timing and whether a human is in the loop now.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Human in the loop, real time → attended. Queue for later/background to optimize resources → unattended.

examPitfalls.title: Pega Robot Manager is separate, not an App Studio nav item
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Lists of App Studio navigation items sometimes slip in 'Robot Manager.'
examPitfalls.bestPractice: App Studio nav = Overview, Case Types, Data, Channels, Library, Users. Robot Manager is a separate control-tower app for monitoring/scheduling robots.

examPitfalls.title: Prediction Studio access requirement
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A detail-level trap: access to Prediction Studio requires a specific portal on the access group.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Remember pxPredictionStudio must be one of the Portals associated with the user's access group.

examPitfalls.title: Layers vs. Rulesets
examPitfalls.trapDescription: These are related but distinct. Layers organize Rules for reuse between applications; Rulesets store/identify Rules that can be shared and reused wholesale.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Think: Layers = stacked application tiers (each built on others, except the Pega Platform Layer); Rulesets = reusable bundles of Rules you can reuse as a whole.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A data scientist needs to build and manage adaptive and predictive machine-learning models for a Pega application. Which studio should they use?

options.text: App Studio
Dev Studio
Prediction Studio
Admin Studio

practiceQuiz.hint: Which studio is specifically the analytics and ML model-building space?
practiceQuiz.rationale: Prediction Studio is the analytics space for adaptive, predictive, and text-analytics models (access requires the pxPredictionStudio portal). App/Dev are authoring spaces; Admin Studio is for system administration.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A System Architect must configure a routine Case process whose capability is fully available in the core low-code authoring space. Per best practice, where should the SA work?

options.text: App Studio, because it manages behind-the-scenes config and reduces errors
Dev Studio, because all SAs must always use Dev Studio
Admin Studio, because SAs administer the system
Prediction Studio, because it generates the rules

practiceQuiz.hint: Default to the studio that reduces programming errors when the feature is available there.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Best practice is to work in App Studio unless a required feature is unavailable; App Studio handles behind-the-scenes configuration and reduces errors. Dev Studio is only for advanced features not available in App Studio.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A new BA opens an existing application to determine its UI architecture. Which TWO statements correctly pair an architecture with its Ruleset?

options.text: Constellation architecture uses the Constellation Ruleset (View-based UI)
Traditional UI architecture uses the Theme Cosmos Ruleset (Section-based UI)
Constellation architecture uses the Theme Cosmos Ruleset
Traditional UI architecture uses the Constellation Ruleset

practiceQuiz.hint: Constellation pairs with Constellation; Traditional pairs with Theme Cosmos.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Constellation = Constellation Ruleset (View-based); Traditional = Theme Cosmos Ruleset (Section-based). Options C and D swap the pairings. No partial credit; both correct answers are needed.

practiceQuiz.scenario: U-Plus Bank must update a customer address in a LEGACY system that exposes no usable API, and a CSR is on the phone with the customer right now. Which approach fits best?

options.text: A standard API connector for real-time exchange
Attended RPA that drives the legacy system's front end in real time
Unattended RPA queued for overnight processing
No integration is possible

practiceQuiz.hint: No API + a human in the loop right now points to one RPA mode.
practiceQuiz.rationale: With no usable API and a CSR actively in the process, attended RPA drives the legacy UI in real time alongside the human. A connector needs a standard protocol (absent here); unattended RPA would defer the update rather than complete it during the call.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A stakeholder asks you to list valid App Studio navigation-pane items. Which THREE of the following are valid?

options.text: Case Types
Channels
Library (Reuse Library)
Robot Manager

practiceQuiz.hint: One option is a separate RPA control-tower application.
practiceQuiz.rationale: App Studio navigation includes Overview, Case Types, Data, Channels, Library, and Users. Pega Robot Manager is a separate application for monitoring/scheduling robots, not a navigation area. No partial credit.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An IT administrator needs runtime information to monitor and debug system resources in production. Which studio is designed for this?

options.text: Admin Studio
App Studio
Prediction Studio
Dev Studio

practiceQuiz.hint: Which studio is the 'control room' for system administration?
practiceQuiz.rationale: Admin Studio is the software-administration space for monitoring and debugging system resources at runtime. App Studio and Dev Studio are authoring environments; Prediction Studio is for analytics models.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which definition best matches the low-code approach as described by Forrester and embodied by Pega?

options.text: Visual, declarative techniques that generate the underlying code as you expand the model
Hand-writing all application logic in Java for maximum control
Outsourcing all development to a third party
Configuring servers from the command line

practiceQuiz.hint: Pega calls its approach 'Software That Writes Your Software' — what technique does that describe?
practiceQuiz.rationale: Low-code uses visual, declarative techniques instead of programming; tools generate code as you expand the model. Hand-writing Java, outsourcing, and command-line server config are not low-code approaches.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A BA names items in App Studio as 'app1', 'process2', and 'field3'. Why is this discouraged?

options.text: Rules are auto-generated with those same names, making them hard to find later
Numeric names crash the Constellation Ruleset
App Studio forbids names containing letters
It disables the Reuse Library

practiceQuiz.hint: Think about what gets generated in the background.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Because Pega auto-generates Rules using the same names you choose, business-friendly names (e.g., 'Send email') make Rules far easier to find. The other claims are fabricated.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which TWO are accurate about co-development between domain experts and implementation experts?

options.text: A Business Analyst can design Views in App Studio while a System Architect adds advanced logic in Dev Studio
Each group works in the environment tailored to their skill level
Only System Architects may touch the application at any time
Domain experts must learn Java before contributing

practiceQuiz.hint: Two environments, two expert groups — how do they complement each other?
practiceQuiz.rationale: Co-development pairs domain experts (App Studio) with implementation experts (Dev Studio), each in an environment suited to them. Domain experts contribute without Java, and development is collaborative — not SA-only. No partial credit.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A standardized approval process built for property insurance should be reused across travel and automobile insurance lines. Where and how is the rule's scope extended for organization-wide reuse?

options.text: In Dev Studio, by extending the rule's scope from one Case Type to a division or the whole organization
In App Studio, by copying the rule into each Case Type manually
In Prediction Studio, by training a model
In Admin Studio, by scheduling a job

practiceQuiz.hint: Extending scope across layers happens in the advanced studio.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Dev Studio accesses all layers and can extend a rule's scope from a single Case Type to an application, division, or organization for reuse. App Studio configures for a single Case Type; Prediction/Admin Studios serve other purposes.

practiceQuiz.scenario: From the App Studio header, a BA wants to capture real-time feedback and track feature development during a stakeholder review. Which tool do they open?

options.text: Pega Agile Workbench
Prediction Studio
Robot Manager
Theme Cosmos

practiceQuiz.hint: It lives in the upper area of App Studio and supports agile feedback.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Pega Agile Workbench (opened from the App Studio header) captures real-time feedback and tracks feature development. Prediction Studio and Robot Manager are separate tools; Theme Cosmos is a Ruleset.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Both systems in an address-update integration understand and support a standard protocol, and the exchange should happen immediately. Which integration choice is most appropriate?

options.text: A standard API connector for real-time exchange
Attended RPA
Unattended RPA
A manual data re-entry process

practiceQuiz.hint: A standard protocol exists → favor the direct option.
practiceQuiz.rationale: When both systems support a standard protocol, a standard API connector exchanges data in real time. RPA is reserved for systems lacking a usable API; manual re-entry defeats automation.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A bank wants address updates processed in the background during off-peak hours to optimize system resources and free CSRs from waiting. Which RPA mode fits?

options.text: Unattended RPA
Attended RPA
A real-time API connector
Prediction Studio scoring

practiceQuiz.hint: The CSR should not wait at their desk; the update can run in the background.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Unattended RPA queues the request for later background processing, optimizing resources and reducing peak loads. Attended RPA runs alongside a human in real time; a connector needs a usable API; Prediction Studio is unrelated.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A team needs to monitor, schedule, and view performance analytics for all of its RPA robots. Which Pega capability provides this control tower?

options.text: Pega Robot Manager
App Studio Library
Admin Studio's Case Type Explorer
The Application profile

practiceQuiz.hint: Its name literally says it manages and monitors robots.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Pega Robot Manager monitors and schedules robots and provides performance analytics. The Library is for reusable assets, the Application profile tracks stories/feedback, and there is no 'Case Type Explorer' control tower for robots.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which THREE statements correctly map App Studio terms to their Dev Studio equivalents?

options.text: Field → Property
Goal and deadline → Service-Level Agreement (SLA)
User → Operator
Channel → Ruleset

practiceQuiz.hint: Three are real App Studio to Dev Studio name mappings; one is invented.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The documented App Studio → Dev Studio mappings are: Field=Property, Goal and deadline=SLA, User=Operator, and Team=Work Group. 'Channel → Ruleset' is not a valid naming equivalence and is a distractor. No partial credit.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A BA needs to delay an SLA's timer start, exclude weekends/holidays, and add an escalation that reassigns the task. Where are these advanced options configured?

options.text: Dev Studio
App Studio
Prediction Studio
Robot Manager

practiceQuiz.hint: These go beyond the basic goal/deadline available in the core studio.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Advanced SLA options — initialization behavior, account-for-business-days, and additional escalation actions like reassign/resolve — are configured in Dev Studio. App Studio offers only the basic goal/deadline; the others are unrelated.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Why can Pega later replace a robotic automation with an API connector with minimal impact once a bank unifies on a modern system of record?

options.text: Because Pega separates application functionality from integration details (data/integration layer separated from the Application layer)
Because robots and connectors are the same Rule type
Because the application logic is duplicated per channel
Because Prediction Studio rewrites the integration automatically

practiceQuiz.hint: Consider how Pega separates application logic from integration details.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Pega separates application functionality from integration details, so the integration mechanism can change (RPA → connector) with minimal application impact. The other options are inaccurate.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A citizen developer wants to confirm whether an application is built on Constellation. Which App Studio element identifies the application type?

options.text: The Application Layers Widget on the overview
The Pulse feed
The Robot Manager dashboard
The Prediction Studio model list

practiceQuiz.hint: It visualizes the Rulesets that make up the app.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The Application Layers Widget visualizes the Rulesets and identifies the application type (Constellation vs. Traditional). You can also confirm via the Application Definition's 'Build on applications' section in Dev Studio.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which TWO are genuine benefits of low-code development as described in the module?

options.text: It creates a common visual language so business and developers collaborate more effectively
It enables omnichannel apps (web, mobile, chatbot) without maintaining disparate code lines
It eliminates the need for any testing
It only works for trivial, spreadsheet-level applications

practiceQuiz.hint: Think about the collaboration benefit and the channel unification benefit.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Low-code provides a common visual language and unifies omnichannel development. It does not eliminate testing, and Pega low-code builds robust (not just trivial) applications. No partial credit.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A user logs into Pega and is immediately placed into one studio, then switches to another using the upper-left menu. Which statement is correct?

options.text: Login opens the user's default studio; they can switch to any studio they have access to
Users can only ever access a single studio
Switching studios requires logging out and back in
Only Admin Studio can be set as a default

practiceQuiz.hint: Default at login, switch via the upper-left menu.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The system opens the user's default studio at login; users with access to multiple studios switch via the upper-left menu without logging out. Access to one OR more studios is configured via Access Group portals.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which statement best distinguishes Layers from Rulesets in App Studio's modular design?

options.text: Layers organize Rules into reusable application tiers (each built on others, except the Pega Platform Layer); Rulesets are reusable bundles of Rules you can reuse as a whole
Layers and Rulesets are identical terms with no difference
Rulesets can only contain a single Rule
Layers exist only in Prediction Studio

practiceQuiz.hint: One is the stack of application tiers; the other is a reusable bundle of Rules.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Layers organize Rules for reuse between applications (each Layer built on one or more others, except the Pega Platform Layer); Rulesets store/identify Rules that can be shared and reused wholesale. The other statements are false.

quickRecap.value: Visual, declarative development that generates code for you — 'Software That Writes Your Software.'
App (core build), Dev (advanced config), Prediction (ML/analytics), Admin (system administration).
Technical users work in App Studio unless a feature is unavailable; then switch to Dev Studio. Login opens your default studio.
Header (incl. upper-left studio switcher + Agile Workbench), Navigation pane (explorers), Authoring space.
Overview, Case Types, Data, Channels, Library (Reuse), Users.
Constellation = Constellation Ruleset (View-based). Traditional = Theme Cosmos Ruleset (Section-based). Identified by the Application Layers Widget.
Field=Property, Goal and deadline=SLA, User=Operator, Team=Work Group.
Connector for standard protocols (real-time). RPA when no usable API: attended (human in loop) vs unattended (queued). Monitor via Pega Robot Manager.
Layers = stacked application tiers (reuse between apps). Rulesets = reusable bundles of Rules reused as a whole.
Initialization behavior, variable interval length, account-for-business-days, extra escalation (reassign/resolve).
